description: Clock-face direction (12/3/6/9 o'clock) spatial reformulations for visual FCI items.
source: Adapted from West-like approach by Ane Kester

items.text:
A ball rolls smoothly through a curved track that forms a half-circle on top of a flat table. Imagine viewing the track from above, with the ball moving from the 9 o'clock position toward the 3 o'clock position. At the moment it reaches the 12 o'clock position, consider the possible forces acting on it:

A) A force pulling straight downward.
B) A force pushing toward 3 o'clock.
C) A force pushing toward 12 o'clock.
D) A force pushing toward 9 o'clock.

Which set of forces is acting on the ball?
1. Force A only
2. Forces A and B
3. Forces A and C
4. Forces A, B, and C
5. Forces A, C, and D

items.text:
A ball rolls through a curved track shaped like part of a circle and then exits onto a perfectly smooth, frictionless tabletop. Imagine viewing the motion from above. At the instant it leaves the track, the ball is moving toward 3 o'clock. Which path will the ball most closely follow after leaving the track?

1. A path that curves gradually toward 12 o'clock.
2. A path that continues straight toward 3 o'clock.
3. A path that curves gradually toward 6 o'clock.
4. A path that curves gradually toward 9 o'clock.
5. A path that immediately heads straight toward 12 o'clock.

items.text:
A steel ball is attached to a string and is swung in a circular path in a horizontal plane. Consider a moment in the ball's motion when the ball is moving toward 12 o'clock. At that moment, the string breaks near the ball. Which of the following paths would the ball most closely follow after the string breaks?

(a) It will initially travel toward 12 o'clock, but will quickly begin to curve toward 9 o'clock.
(b) It will travel toward 12 o'clock in a straight line.
(c) It will travel toward 1:30 in a straight line.
(d) It will initially travel toward 3 o'clock, but will quickly begin to curve toward 12 o'clock.
(e) It will travel toward 3 o'clock in a straight line.

items.text:
A hockey puck is sliding with constant speed v_0 toward 3 o'clock on a frictionless horizontal surface. Forces from the air are negligible. When the puck reaches a certain point, it receives a swift horizontal kick toward 12 o'clock. If the puck had been at rest when it received this kick, it would have started moving toward 12 o'clock with a speed v_k.

Which path will the puck most closely follow after receiving the kick?

1. It will travel straight toward 12 o'clock.
2. It will travel in a straight line toward 1:30.
3. It will continue straight toward 3 o'clock, after a shift toward 12 o'clock.
4. It will curve gradually toward 12 o'clock.
5. It will start moving toward 12 o'clock, then curve gradually toward 3 o'clock.

items.text:
A ball is launched horizontally from the top of a cliff, from a cannon pointing toward 3 o'clock. The flat ground below extends toward 3 o'clock from the cliff base. Air resistance is negligible. The ball lands on the ground some distance toward 3 o'clock from the base.

Which path will the ball most closely follow?

1. A straight diagonal line from the launch point to the landing point.
2. A smooth curve downward from the launch point to the landing point.
3. Straight toward 3 o'clock for a short distance, then curving downward to the landing point.
4. Straight toward 3 o'clock for some distance, then curved, then vertical some time before landing.
5. Straight toward 3 o'clock until nearly above the landing point, then vertical to the ground.

items.text:
A bowling ball falls from the cargo bay of an airplane flying toward 3 o'clock in a straight, level path. Air resistance is negligible. An observer on the ground, watching from the 6 o'clock direction, watches the ball after it leaves the airplane.

Which path will the ball most closely follow?

1. A curve going toward 9 o'clock and toward the ground.
2. Straight down toward the ground.
3. A straight line aimed down toward 3 o'clock.
4. A curve going toward 3 o'clock and toward the ground.
5. Straight toward 3 o'clock for a while, then straight toward the ground.

items.text:
A child swings on a rope tied to a branch (point O). His movement starts above a point A and then continues downward through the point A. Consider the following distinct forces:
1. A downward force of gravity.
2. A force exerted by the rope pointing from A to O.
3. A force in the direction of the boy's motion.
4. A force pointing from O to A.
Which of the above forces is (are) acting on the boy when he is at position A?
(A) 1 only.
(B) 1 and 2.
(C) 1 and 3.
(D) 1, 2, and 3.
(E) 1, 3, and 4.

items.text:
Two blocks move along the same straight track in the same direction. Positions are measured every 0.2 s in length units (LU). Times t_1, t_2, t_3, ... indicate the same moments for both blocks.

Block A: t_1: 2 LU, t_2: 4 LU, t_3: 7 LU, t_4: 11 LU, t_5: 16 LU, t_6: 22 LU, t_7: 29 LU
Block B: t_1: 0 LU, t_2: 4 LU, t_3: 8 LU, t_4: 12 LU, t_5: 16 LU, t_6: 20 LU, t_7: 24 LU, t_8: 28 LU

Do the blocks ever have the same speed?

1. No.
2. Yes, at instant t_2.
3. Yes, at instant t_5.
4. Yes, at instants t_2 and t_5.
5. Yes, at some time during the interval t_3 to t_4.

items.text:
A rocket drifts in outer space from point A to point B, moving toward 3 o'clock. Starting at position B, the rocket's engine is turned on and produces a constant thrust toward 12 o'clock. This thrust is maintained until the rocket reaches a point C.

Which path below best represents the path of the rocket between points B and C?

1. Point C lies at about 1:30 from point B. The path from B to C starts toward 12 o'clock, and curves smoothly toward 3 o'clock.
2. Point C lies at 12 o'clock from point B. The path from B to C is straight toward 12 o'clock.
3. Point C lies at about 1:30 from point B. The path from B to C is straight.
4. Point C lies at about 1:30 from point B. The path from B to C continues toward 3 o'clock for a bit, then curves toward 12 o'clock, then continues straight toward 1:30.
5. Point C lies at about 1:30 from point B. The path from B to C starts toward 3 o'clock, and curves smoothly toward 12 o'clock.
